flags: minor: overlaps thematically with R032-08 and R032-09 (all turn on 'noticing vs. copying/explaining'); R032-09's key ('attends to the dough rather than copying Lena') points toward this item's answer
R032-01.notes: Para 7 'could not be explained, only noticed' and the closing lines support C. A and D are directly contradicted (explanation and watching both failed); B misreads Lena's silence as disapproval, which the 'There' scene refutes.

flags: minor: the step from 'see what four in the morning looked like' to 'learn something by experiencing it firsthand' is an inference from the whole passage; B is defensible mainly because the other choices have no support
R032-02.notes: 'I did not yet know that she meant this as a kindness' and the later key, early mornings and 'bowl of my own to ruin' show Lena meant firsthand experience. A is a trap for readers who take the line as discouragement; C and D have no textual basis.

R032-03.notes: The saying is reread as 'more like a warning': the first hundred are only practice, so mastery will take long. A, B and C have no support (the father's job is irrelevant to choosing the bakery, and he never comments on the job).

R032-04.notes: Context is tacky to smooth and then 'push back' as a sign of readiness. This is the elasticity of a well-kneaded dough, so the baking fact is accurate. B (refusing to be shaped) is the literal-reading trap; C and D are unsupported.

R032-05.notes: This fits Lena's unannounced way of giving and para 7 ('What she had given me instead was the key'). D fails on timing (the key came the week before the success). C is a mild trap. A is unsupported.

flags: minor: the wrong choices are weak; B is contradicted by 'not at her' and C is the opposite of the tone, so few students would pick them
R032-06.notes: Hiding a failed batch that 'I hoped nobody would ask about' shows embarrassment.

R032-07.notes: 'unmarked among hers' plus 'without looking twice' means the loaves were indistinguishable. D is the opposite. C overreaches. B has no support.

flags: minor: overlaps with R032-01 (both rest on 'could not be explained, only noticed')
R032-08.notes: Para 2 reads 'It tells you' as what adults say when they do not want to explain, which is an evasion. Para 7 says the thing could only be noticed, so the statement was accurate. The starting halves of A, B and D do not match para 2.

flags: minor: the key closely paraphrases para 5 ('instead of copying her hands, paid attention to my own... I did not hurry'), so this is close to a lookup
minor: overlaps with R032-01 and its wording helps answer R032-01
R032-09.notes: A is the opposite. C distorts the father's saying (it never advises working fast). D is unsupported.

R032-10.notes: The passage explains the causes of the heat island, then weighs coatings and trees. A is too narrow and too strong (the passage notes that reflective roofs have drawbacks). C and D are not in the passage. Science check: nighttime peak on calm, clear nights; reduction by wind and clouds; evapotranspiration cooling; the winter penalty of reflective roofs. All are accurate.

R032-11.notes: It follows a contrast: coatings are quick, and trees are slow but give lasting shade and cooling. Doing both pairs their strengths. B is the trap, and it is contradicted by 'Researchers continue to argue'. A and D are unsupported.
